verdict.label: serious_barriers
verdict.headline: Keyboard users cannot get past the cookie banner, and screen reader users cannot find the cart, so neither group can buy.
verdict.summary: We checked 38 pages and found 12 problems. 2 of them stop people from buying: the cookie banner traps the keyboard, and the cart button has no name a screen reader can read. Most problems come from 4 shared page parts, such as the site header and the product layout, so each one repeats across many pages. Headings and page structure are clear throughout. 4 more items need a person to confirm them.

groups.summary: Cannot find the cart and get stuck in the cookie banner, so they cannot buy.
Lose prices and buttons when zooming, and cannot read faint text.
Cannot get past the cookie banner and cannot see where they are on the page.

journeys.name: Find a store
journeys.not_tested_reason: the store finder did not load

priorities.reason: Problems that block buying come first, then those on every page, then those on the product pages.

issues.severity_reason: Stops every task on the site on a first visit; there is no way around it.
issues.title: Keyboard users get stuck in the cookie banner

where.summary: Cookie banner, shown on the first visit to any page

issues.observed: When the banner opens, the Tab key moves only between its “Settings” and “Privacy” links. The “Accept” and “Reject” buttons are skipped, and the banner cannot be closed.
issues.cause: The banner holds the keyboard inside itself, as pop-ups do. Its two buttons are built from plain boxes the keyboard cannot reach, so there is no way out.

impacts.text: They cannot close the banner, so they cannot use any page of the site.
They hear the two links over and over and never reach the buttons, so they cannot continue.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the cookie banner at the bottom of the home page. The “Accept” and “Reject” buttons, marked 1 and 2, cannot be reached with the keyboard.
shots.caption: Cookie banner on the home page. Buttons 1 and 2 cannot be reached with the Tab key.

steps: Rebuild “Accept” and “Reject” as real buttons, so the Tab key reaches them.
Let the Escape key close the banner and return to the page.
fix.dev_note: Use native button elements; keep focus inside the dialog only while it is open.
fix.done_when: With only the keyboard, you can open any page, reach “Reject”, press Enter and carry on browsing.

issues.severity_reason: Blocks checkout for screen reader users on every page.
issues.title: The cart button has no name screen readers can read
issues.observed: The cart icon in the top right opens the cart, but a screen reader announces it only as “button”. The number of items in the cart is not read out either.
issues.cause: The icon is a picture inside a plain box with no text name, so software cannot tell what it is or what it does.

impacts.text: They hear only “button”, so they cannot find their cart or go to checkout.
Saying “click cart” in voice control does nothing, because the button has no name to say.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the site header. The cart icon in the top right is highlighted; it has no name a screen reader can read.
shots.caption: Site header. The highlighted cart icon has no readable name.

steps: Rebuild the cart icon as a real button.
Give it a hidden text name with the item count, such as “Cart, 2 items”.
fix.dev_note: A native button with visually hidden text; update the text whenever the count changes.
fix.done_when: With a screen reader on, the icon is announced as “Cart, 2 items, button”.

issues.severity_reason: Buying is possible, but only by guessing what the product looks like.
issues.title: Product photos have no text description

where.summary: Product photos on the product page type

issues.observed: 214 product photos show colour, pattern and fit, but none has a text description. Screen readers often read out the file name instead, such as “IMG 4471 jpg”.
issues.cause: The product layout adds each photo without a text description (alt text). Every product uses the same layout, so the gap repeats on every product page.

impacts.text: They hear a file name instead of a description, so they cannot judge colour or style before buying.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the product grid. Three product photos, marked 1 to 3, have no text description.
shots.caption: Product grid on a category page. Photos 1 to 3 have no text description.

steps: Add a short text description to every product photo that says what it shows.
Mark purely decorative images as decorative.
fix.dev_note: Fill the alt attribute from a product field editors can maintain; decorative images get alt="".
fix.done_when: A screen reader reads a useful description for each product photo.

issues.severity_reason: Buying needs sideways scrolling or help for people who zoom.
issues.title: Price and “Add to cart” are cut off on narrow screens

where.summary: Product grid on the product and category page types

issues.observed: In a window 320 pixels wide, or at 400 % zoom, the product grid keeps four columns. The price and the “Add to cart” button of most products fall outside the screen.
issues.cause: The grid always has four columns. When there is no room, it does not move the products below each other, so the part that does not fit is hidden.

impacts.text: The price and the buy button vanish when they enlarge the page, so they cannot buy without help.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the product grid at normal width, with four products in a row.
shots.caption: Product grid at normal width and at phone width.
shots.label: Normal width (1280 pixels)

pair.alt: Screenshot of the same grid 320 pixels wide. The highlighted price is cut off at the edge of the screen.
pair.label: Phone width (320 pixels)

steps: Let the product grid drop to one or two columns on narrow screens.
fix.dev_note: Use a responsive grid such as repeat(auto-fill, minmax(…)) instead of four fixed columns.
fix.done_when: At 400 % zoom every price and button is visible without sideways scrolling.

issues.severity_reason: Every task is possible but slow and error-prone without a mouse.
issues.title: The keyboard highlight is invisible on menu links

where.summary: Main menu in the site header, on every page

issues.observed: When the Tab key reaches a menu link such as “Sale”, nothing on screen changes. The page looks the same as before the key was pressed.
issues.cause: The site styling removes the browser’s outline around the selected link and puts nothing in its place.

impacts.text: They cannot see which link is selected, so they press Enter on the wrong one or give up.
Losing their place on the page adds effort to every step.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the main menu before the Tab key is pressed.
shots.caption: Main menu before and after the Tab key reaches “Sale”.
shots.label: Before: pointer on the page

pair.alt: Screenshot of the main menu after the Tab key reaches “Sale”. The highlighted link looks exactly as before.
pair.label: After: “Sale” reached with the Tab key

steps: Show a clear, thick outline around any link or button the keyboard reaches.
fix.dev_note: Add a :focus-visible style with at least 3:1 contrast against the background.
fix.done_when: Pressing Tab on any page always shows where you are.

issues.severity_reason: Signing up is very hard without knowing what went wrong.
issues.title: Form errors are shown only by a red colour
issues.observed: When an email address is wrong, the field turns red and a red dot appears below it. There is no text saying what is wrong.
issues.cause: The error is shown by colour alone, with no words, so people who cannot see red or cannot see the screen get no message.

impacts.text: They see a grey border and no message, so they do not know why the form will not send.
Nothing is read out, so they do not know the form failed.
With no words to explain the error, they have to guess what to change.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the newsletter form after a wrong email address. The highlighted error is a red dot with no text.
shots.caption: Newsletter form after sending a wrong email address.

steps: Add a short text message to each error, such as “Enter an email address like name@example.com”.
fix.dev_note: Connect the message to the field so screen readers announce it.
fix.done_when: A wrong entry shows a written message, and a screen reader reads it.

issues.severity_reason: Forms can be completed, but with more effort and mistakes.
issues.title: Hint text in form fields is too faint to read
issues.observed: The pale grey hint text inside the fields, such as “Email address”, barely stands out from the white background.
issues.cause: All forms share one style for hint text, and that style uses a very light grey.

impacts.text: The hints look blank, so they cannot tell what each field asks for.
Unclear fields lead to mistakes and having to start again.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the newsletter form. The highlighted email field shows a hint text that is very hard to see.
shots.caption: Email field on the newsletter form.

steps: Darken the hint text until it reaches the required contrast.
fix.dev_note: Change the placeholder colour to at least #767676 on white.
fix.done_when: The hint text measures at least 4.5 to 1 against its background.

issues.severity_reason: Important terms are hard to read, but the text is still there.
issues.title: Footer text is too faint to read
issues.observed: The footer text, including “Returns within 60 days” and “Prices include VAT”, is light grey on an almost white background.
issues.cause: The footer style uses a light grey text colour that is too close to its background.

impacts.text: They cannot read the return and price terms without copying the text or zooming in.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the site footer. The highlighted text is light grey on a near-white background.
shots.caption: Site footer.

steps: Use a darker text colour in the footer.
fix.dev_note: Set the footer text colour to #595959 or darker on #FAFAFA.
fix.done_when: The footer text measures at least 4.5 to 1.

issues.severity_reason: Information is lost, but it is repeated elsewhere on the site.
issues.title: The founders’ video has no captions

where.summary: Home page and About page (the same video on both)

issues.observed: In the 2-minute video “Meet the founders”, everything is spoken, including the 60-day return promise. There are no captions and no written version on the page.
issues.cause: The video was published without a caption file, so the player has no captions to show.

impacts.text: They see people talking but miss what they say, including the return promise.
They lose parts of the spoken message and have no text to check it against.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the video player on the home page, showing the start screen of the video “Meet the founders”.
shots.caption: Video on the home page. It has no captions.

steps: Add a short written summary or transcript below it.
fix.dev_note: Upload a captions track (WebVTT) to the video host and check its accuracy.
fix.done_when: Captions can be switched on and match what is said.

issues.severity_reason: People can still shop, but finding and comparing products takes longer.
issues.title: All product pages have the same page title
issues.observed: All 24 product pages are titled “Northwind Outdoor”. The browser tab and search results never name the product.
issues.cause: The product layout uses the shop name as the page title instead of the product name.

impacts.text: The first thing they hear on each page is the same, so they cannot tell product pages apart.
Several open tabs look identical, which makes comparing products confusing.

steps: Put the product name first in each product page title, such as “Trail runner 2 – Northwind Outdoor”.
fix.done_when: Each product tab shows its product name.

issues.severity_reason: An annoyance: the wrong page opens, but people can retry.
issues.title: Page number buttons are very small
issues.observed: The page number buttons under the product lists are 16 by 16 pixels and touch each other.
issues.cause: The pagination style uses small, tightly packed boxes for the page numbers.

impacts.text: They often tap the wrong page number and have to try again.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the page numbers under a product list. The four highlighted buttons are very small and touch each other.
shots.caption: Page numbers under a product list.

steps: Make each page number at least 24 by 24 pixels, or add space between them.
fix.done_when: Each page number is easy to tap on a phone.

issues.severity_reason: The text can still be read, but pronunciation may be wrong.
issues.title: Two pages do not say which language they are in
issues.observed: The Privacy and Shipping pages do not state that they are in English.
issues.cause: These two pages come from an older layout that does not set the page language.

impacts.text: Their screen reader may read the English text with the wrong pronunciation.

steps: Set the page language to English on both pages.
fix.dev_note: Add lang="en" to the html element.
fix.done_when: Both pages state their language in the page code.

review_items.title: Check whether product photo descriptions say what the photo shows

where.summary: Product page type, once descriptions are added

review_items.observed: Some product photos on newer pages have descriptions such as “Product image”. They do not say what the photo shows.
review_items.why_uncertain: Only someone who knows the products can judge whether a description is accurate.
review_items.what_to_check: Someone who knows the products compares each photo with its description. Generic or wrong descriptions are a problem.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the product grid. The first photo is highlighted.
shots.caption: Product photo with a generic description.

review_items.title: Check whether the store finder map has a text alternative
review_items.observed: The store finder shows shop locations on an embedded map. We could not find a list of shops in text.
review_items.why_uncertain: The page did not finish loading during the review, so we could not see all of it.
review_items.what_to_check: Open the store finder and check that every shop's address is also listed in text.

shots.alt: Screenshot of the banner area of the home page, where the store finder is linked.
shots.caption: Banner on the home page that links to the store finder.

review_items.title: Check whether the checkout time limit can be extended
review_items.observed: The checkout says items are reserved for 10 minutes. We did not see a way to ask for more time.
review_items.why_uncertain: We did not wait for the time limit to run out, so we do not know what happens then.
review_items.what_to_check: Start a checkout, wait 10 minutes and check whether the site warns you and lets you extend the time.

review_items.title: Check whether “Read more” links make sense on the journal pages
review_items.observed: Each journal teaser ends with a “Read more” link. The heading next to it may be enough to explain it.
review_items.why_uncertain: Whether the nearby heading explains the link depends on how it is read.
review_items.what_to_check: Read each “Read more” link with its heading and check that it is clear which article it opens.

glossary.meaning: Software that reads the screen aloud, or shows it on a braille display, for people who cannot see it.
A short text description of an image, read out by screen readers. You can usually edit it in your content manager.
How much text stands out from its background, measured as a ratio such as 4.5 to 1.
The outline that shows which link or button the keyboard has reached. Developers call it the focus indicator.
On-screen text of what is said in a video and of important sounds.
The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international standard for accessible websites. Level AA is the level most laws refer to.
